name: judge-keep-warm
description: Keeps a session's prompt cache warm and, when the cache is about to expire, files the thread into a GitHub manifest that it bundles into projects itself, through your own Claude Code connection, so you resume threads instead of opening new ones

manifest_repo.title: Manifest repository
manifest_repo.description: The GitHub repository that holds the thread manifest, as owner/repo; private, with the token given Contents read and write on it. Default: judgedice/judgeiverse. Empty: threads are not filed.

account_label.title: Account label
account_label.description: How this Claude Code account is named in the manifest (work, personal, ...). Empty: the machine's user and host name.

github_token.title: GitHub token
github_token.description: A fine-grained token with Contents read and write on the manifest repository. Empty: the JUDGE_KEEP_WARM_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN variable, else the gh CLI's login.

file_threads.title: File threads in the manifest
file_threads.description: When the cache is about to expire, write this thread's entry to the manifest repository. Off: only /judge file writes one.

judge_model.title: Judge model
judge_model.description: The model that bundles the threads into projects when a thread is filed: an alias (haiku, sonnet, opus) or a full id. Empty: this session's own model.

title_mark.title: Mark the session title
title_mark.description: While keep-warm is on, put a green dot in front of the session's title in the desktop app's session list

sweep_deleted.title: Take deleted threads out of the manifest
sweep_deleted.description: When a thread this machine filed has had its session deleted (its transcript is gone from ~/.claude/projects), take it out of the manifest and keep a one-line summary in its project's sub-manifest. Never runs in a cloud container, where transcripts do not persist. Entries deleted from the repository by hand are taken out either way.
